title: Plain Flask UI routes need an explicit authenticated-only validator or the fail-closed net denies non-admins
answers: non-admin user sees 'Permission denied' instead of the MLflow UI in basic-auth
basic-auth web UI unreachable for RBAC users with fail-closed authorization
GET / returns 403 for users without is_admin
MLflow UI blank or denied for workspace MANAGE users
body:
Symptom: with basic-auth and fail-closed authorization on, a signed-in user without the server-wide is_admin flag gets a plain 'Permission denied' at the server root instead of the UI; RBAC grants do not help.
Root cause: mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py:_before_request denies any route with no authorization decision. '/', '/version' and the ui-telemetry routes are plain Flask routes on app, so get_endpoints() never registers them with the coverage guard.
Fix pattern: add each such route to the route-to-validator map in mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py as _allow_authenticated. Bare paths take _add_static_prefix at the call site (HOME, SERVER_VERSION in mlflow/server/auth/routes.py); UI_TELEMETRY is already prefixed by _get_ajax_path.
Constraints: this keeps authentication required and skips only the authorization decision. Do not place these in _UNPROTECTED_PATH_PREFIXES or is_unprotected_route, which short-circuit before authenticate_request and drop the login requirement. Self-service signup and GET /api/3.0/mlflow/workspaces/<name> were deliberately left denied.
Applies: any new plain Flask route on app under basic-auth that must serve the UI or a non-tenant string to signed-in users.
applies: basic-auth (--app-name basic-auth) with fail-closed authorization enabled; plain Flask routes registered on app rather than handler endpoints.
says: Non-admin users see a permission denied error when opening the home page.
Members with workspace manage access cannot load the web dashboard after logging in.
Allow authenticated team members without full administrator roles to view the web console.
The tracking server UI fails to display for signed-in users using username password authentication.
Regular logged-in users should reach the portal rather than getting blocked at the root URL.
search: Under basic-auth with fail-closed authorization, plain Flask routes on app must be registered with _allow_authenticated in mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py to prevent non-admins from receiving 403 errors. Bare paths like HOME ('/') and SERVER_VERSION ('/version') take _add_static_prefix at the call site, while UI_TELEMETRY is prefixed by _get_ajax_path; self-service signup and GET /api/3.0/mlflow/workspaces/<name> remain denied. Routes must not be added to _UNPROTECTED_PATH_PREFIXES or is_unprotected_route, which drop the login requirement.
